rejected.title: Managing the Great Barrier Reef
card: Marine park
The Great Barrier Reef is protected as a marine park. The Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority, a federal government body, manages it with the Queensland Government.
Zoning
The park is split into zones with different rules. Some zones limit or ban fishing so that fish and coral can recover. Other zones allow more uses.
Local actions
Managers work with farmers to cut the soil and fertiliser that wash onto the reef. They also control crown-of-thorns starfish, which eat coral.
Global limit
These actions reduce local pressures. Warming seas come from global greenhouse gas emissions, so the reef's future depends most on cutting emissions worldwide.
rejected.remember: Local actions ease some pressures on the reef, but cutting global emissions matters most for its future.

a.q: What is the main purpose of the different zones in the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park?
opts: To set different rules for different areas, such as fishing limits
To keep all people out of the whole reef area
To mark which areas farmers may use for crops
To stop the seas from warming in each area
a.why: Zones give different areas different rules, and some limit or ban fishing so that fish and coral can recover. Zones do not keep everyone out, because other zones allow more uses.
a.clue: Think about what a zone does to rules in each area.

b.q: Reef managers cut farm runoff and control starfish for years, but sea temperatures keep rising. Why does the reef's future still depend most on global action?
opts: Warming comes from global emissions, which reef managers cannot cut
Runoff and starfish are not a threat to the reef
Marine park zones cannot limit any fishing
Governments are not allowed to manage the reef
b.why: Warming seas come from global greenhouse gas emissions, and local managers cannot cut those. Local actions still help by easing other pressures, so the tempting idea that they are pointless is wrong.
b.clue: Where does the cause of warming seas come from?

a.q: What is the main purpose of the different zones in the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park?
opts: To allow some uses in one area but limit them in another
To keep all people out of every part of the reef
To show farmers which coastal areas they may plant
To stop the sea from warming in the protected areas
a.why: Each zone has its own rules, so some limit or ban fishing while others allow more uses. Zones do not keep everyone out of the whole reef, and they cannot stop warming, which comes from global emissions.

Farm runoff from Queensland is what warms the sea
Stricter fishing zones could stop the sea from warming
b.why: Warming seas are caused by greenhouse gas emissions from all over the world, so local work cannot fix them. It is tempting to think local actions are pointless, but they do ease other pressures such as runoff and starfish.
b.clue: Where do the gases that warm the sea come from?

version.title: Managing the Great Barrier Reef
card: Marine park
The Great Barrier Reef is protected as a marine park. The Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority, a federal government body, manages it with the Queensland Government.
Zoning
The park is split into zones with different rules. Some zones limit or ban fishing so that fish and coral can recover. Other zones allow more uses.
Local actions
Managers work with farmers to cut the soil and fertiliser that wash onto the reef. They also control crown-of-thorns starfish, which eat coral.
Global limit
These actions reduce local pressures. Warming seas come from global greenhouse gas emissions, so the reef's future depends most on cutting emissions worldwide.
version.remember: Local actions ease some pressures on the reef, but cutting global emissions matters most for its future.

a.q: What is the main purpose of the different zones in the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park?
opts: To set different rules on fishing and other uses by area
To close every part of the reef to all boats and visitors
To track where crown-of-thorns starfish are spreading
To cool the water in each area so that coral can recover
a.why: Zones give different parts of the park different rules. Some limit or ban fishing so fish and coral can recover, while others allow more uses. Zones do not close the whole reef, and they cannot cool the water, because warming comes from global emissions.
a.clue: Think about what changes as you move from one zone to the next.

b.q: Reef managers cut farm runoff and control starfish for years, but sea temperatures keep rising. Why does the reef's future still depend most on global action?
opts: Warming seas come from emissions made all over the world
Runoff and starfish cause most of the warming in the sea
Local actions have made the reef's other threats worse
Australia's own emissions are the only cause of warming
b.why: Warming seas come from greenhouse gas emissions around the world, so reef managers cannot fix them locally. Cutting runoff and controlling starfish ease other pressures, but they do not cause or stop the warming.
b.clue: Ask whether reef managers can reach the cause of the heat.

a.best: To set different rules on fishing and other uses by area

b.best: Warming seas come from emissions made all over the world
